refuted_claims: That the awk read the whole program path. It split on /[ ;]/, so a unit running `<dir>/run.sh evil` read as running the declared `<dir>/run.sh`, hashed the declared file, and exited 0 over the wrong program. The separator is systemd's own ` ; ` now.
That the divergence marker tells the operator what runs. cli::check prints a failing script's stderr under exit 1 and the marker was on stdout only; it goes to both now.

That FALSIFY-EXEC-005 named a real mutation and FALSIFY-EXEC-006 tested its prediction. 005 described an exit code the shell never reads; 006 cited only the parse-time refusal. Reworded, and the runtime half added as a case.
That the contract's converged was 'every declared obligation holds' and that check reports 'N obligations, 0 failed'. Presence is part of convergence and check reports markers and an exit code.
That the book's marker 'names what the unit runs' held for the digest marker, and that validate refuses any non-hex digest. The digest marker names a digest, and a template is left to the resolver.
That no program path defeats the parse. A path containing ` ; ` is misread (divergent, the failing direction) — now the stated limit.

systems: systemd (the manager's loaded unit, drop-ins folded in, is what `systemctl show` reports; the unit file is not)
Kubernetes (an image referenced by `@sha256:` digest is pulled and verified by digest; a tag is a pointer)
Nix (a store path's identity is the hash of its contents, not its name)
Sigstore / in-toto (verify the artifact, not the pointer to it)
Ansible and Puppet (a present-but-wrong resource is a change, not a no-op)
crux.verdict: accept(every surveyed system that cares what executes identifies it by content and asks the thing that runs it: Kubernetes pins images by digest, Nix names paths by hash, Sigstore verifies the artifact. forjar asked presence questions of the unit and none of the program. Where forjar is WEAKER after this change: it verifies argv[0] of the first ExecStart only, where a digest-pinned container image covers everything the entrypoint loads — a wrapper script that execs an undeclared second script is still unverified. Where it is stronger than a lint over the unit file: it reads the manager, so a drop-in or a hand edit is seen.)
